name: Turning effects of forces and moments

questions.q: What scientific term is used to describe the turning effect of a force?
What is the formula used to calculate the moment of a force?
a: Moment = Force multiplied by Perpendicular Distance from pivot

questions.q: What are the standard SI units for a moment of a force?
What is a pivot (or fulcrum) in the context of turning forces?
a: The heaviest part of a moving object
The total surface area of contact
The speed at which a lever rotates
The fixed point or axis about which a body turns or rotates

questions.q: According to the principle of moments, what condition must be met for a seesaw or lever to be balanced in equilibrium?
a: Total clockwise moments equal total anticlockwise moments
The force on both sides must be zero
The distance from the pivot must be identical on both sides
Total mass must be distributed randomly

questions.q: Why are door handles placed as far away as possible from the door hinges (pivot)?
a: To make the door look larger
To increase the distance from the pivot, which reduces the force needed to open the door (creates a larger moment)
To increase friction against the frame
To keep handles out of reach of small children

questions.q: If a child applies a force of 200 N at a distance of 1.5 metres from a playground seesaw pivot, what is the turning moment?
Which of the following is a classic everyday example of a first-class lever where the pivot is located between the effort force and the load?
What happens to the turning moment if you double the distance of the applied force from the pivot while keeping the force the same?
Why is it much easier to loosen a tight rusty nut using a long spanner (wrench) rather than a short one?
a: Long spanners are made of stronger metal
A longer spanner increases the distance from the pivot, producing a greater turning moment for the same push
A long spanner reduces friction on the thread
It adds extra weight to the bolt

questions.q: What term describes the single point through which the entire weight of an object appears to act?
a: The centre of gravity (or centre of mass)

questions.q: How can you increase the stability of a tall object, such as a laboratory Bunsen burner or a racing car?
a: By making it much taller and narrower
By placing all the heavy parts at the very top
By lowering its centre of gravity and widening its base

questions.q: Which of the following describes a second-class lever, such as a wheelbarrow or bottle opener?
a: The load is located between the pivot and the effort force
The effort force is in the middle between the load and pivot
The pivot is always at the very end

questions.q: What happens to an object if its centre of gravity moves outside its base when tilted?
a: It returns automatically to its original position
It topples over because gravity creates an unbalanced turning moment

questions.q: If a wrench produces a moment of 50 N m with a force of 25 N, how far from the pivot is the force applied?
Which of the following is an example of a third-class lever, where the effort force is applied between the load and the pivot?
a: A pair of tweezers or fishing rod

questions.q: Why do crane operators place heavy concrete blocks at the back of a construction crane?
a: To act as a counterweight that balances the heavy loads lifted at the front, preventing the crane from tipping over
To anchor the crane into the clouds
To provide electricity to the motor
To make the crane look decorative

questions.q: What is the turning effect if two equal forces act on opposite sides of a pivot at equal distances, one pushing clockwise and the other anticlockwise?
a: The object spins rapidly in circles
The total net moment is zero, so the system is balanced

questions.q: Why is a racing car designed to have a very low profile (sitting low to the ground) and wide wheels?
a: To make it travel slower around corners
To lower its centre of gravity, making it much more stable and less likely to roll over at high speeds

questions.q: What happens to the stability of a bus if too many passengers stand on the upper deck?
a: Its centre of gravity is lowered, increasing stability
Its centre of gravity is raised, making it less stable and more likely to tip over when turning corners

questions.q: If a heavy box is pushed across a floor, under what condition will it tip over rather than slide?
a: When the line of action of its weight falls outside its base
When the floor becomes completely smooth
When gravity stops acting on it

questions.q: How does a nutcracker make it easier to crack a hard nutshell?
a: It acts as a lever where the short distance from the pivot to the nut multiplies the applied force
It shatters the shell using sound waves
It cuts the shell with lasers

questions.q: What is the moment produced if a force of 10 N is applied 0.4 metres away from a pivot?
Which of the following objects has the lowest centre of gravity and is therefore exceptionally stable?
a: A pencil standing vertically on its tip

questions.q: Why are steering wheels in cars made relatively large in diameter?
a: To provide a larger radius from the steering column pivot, reducing the force the driver needs to apply to turn the wheels
To give more legroom to the driver

questions.q: If a seesaw has a 300 N child sitting 2 metres from the pivot on the left, what force must a 600 N adult exert on the right side to balance the seesaw?
What term describes the perpendicular distance from the line of action of a force to the pivot?
Why do tightrope walkers carry a long, heavy pole while walking across a high rope?
a: To provide shade from the sun
To increase their rotational inertia and lower/shift their centre of gravity, making it easier to balance

questions.q: What happens to a balanced lever if the clockwise moment becomes greater than the anticlockwise moment?
a: The lever starts to rotate in the clockwise direction

questions.q: Which simple machine uses a wheel and axle to make turning heavy valves or doorknobs easier?
a: A lever system where a small force on a large wheel radius turns a smaller axle with a larger force

questions.q: What condition must be satisfied for a physical object to be in complete mechanical equilibrium?
a: Both resultant force must be zero and resultant moment must be zero
The object must be traveling at the speed of light

questions.q: Why is it harder to push a heavy door open near its hinges compared to pushing near the outer edge?
a: The door is thicker near the hinges
Friction is higher near the frame
The distance from the pivot is very small, resulting in a tiny turning moment

questions.q: If a force of 40 N is applied to a spanner at a distance of 0.5 m from a bolt, what is the turning moment?
How does a crowbar help a worker lift heavy paving stones?
a: By acting as a long lever that multiplies the input force into a large moment at the load end

questions.q: What happens to the centre of gravity of a person when they bend forward to touch their toes?
a: It moves upward into their head
It shifts forward, and as long as it stays above their feet, they will not fall over
It moves backward behind their heels
